MBE 考点解析：私人妨害 (Private Nuisance)

本题考察的是侵权法（Torts）中关于私人妨害（Private Nuisance）的核心构成要件。正确答案是 B。

核心法律规则：
私人妨害是指对原告使用和享用其土地的利益进行了实质性（Substantial）且不合理（Unreasonable）的干涉。

1. 法律要件详解

要赢得私人妨害的诉讼，原告必须同时证明以下两点：

  • 实质性干涉 (Substantial Interference)：
    这是一个客观标准（Objective Standard）。干涉必须是具有正常感受力的人（Person of normal sensibilities）都会觉得冒犯、烦恼或无法忍受的。
    注意：如果原告是因为过度敏感（Hypersensitivity）而感到被打扰，则不构成实质性干涉。
  • 不合理干涉 (Unreasonable Interference)：
    法院会进行利益衡量（Balancing Test）。必须证明原告所受伤害的严重程度（Gravity of harm）超过了被告行为的社会效用（Utility of conduct）。

2. 案情分析

在本案中，退休夫妇习惯于安静的下午（读书、听古典乐、午睡）。隔壁孩子们的游泳池噪音打扰了他们。虽然这对夫妇确实感到被打扰，但法律不仅看他们是否被打扰，还要看这种打扰是否满足上述两个法律要件。

为什么 B 是正确答案？
选项 B 准确地指出了胜诉的两个前提：

  1. 噪音必须达到实质性（Substantial）程度，即必须能打扰到“正常感受力的人”，而不仅仅是这对可能喜静的退休夫妇。
  2. 噪音必须是不合理（Unreasonable）的。
这直接排除了因原告“特殊敏感性”而胜诉的可能性，符合 Private Nuisance 的定义。

3. 为什么其他选项是错误的？

选项 A 错误

理由： 法律并不赋予“儿童玩耍”绝对的优先权。虽然儿童玩耍有社会效用（Utility），但必须与邻居的安宁利益进行权衡（Balancing），不能一概而论。

选项 C 错误

理由： 虽然“先来后到”（Coming to the nuisance）是法院考虑的一个因素，但它不是决定性因素。仅仅因为夫妇住得久，并不意味着他们拥有禁止邻居合理使用土地的绝对否决权。

选项 D 错误（高干扰项）

理由： 选项 D 只提到了“实质性干涉”（Substantial Interference），却漏掉了“不合理性”（Unreasonableness）这一关键要件。即使噪音很大（实质性），如果其社会效用极高且无法避免，也可能不构成妨害。此外，D 没有明确强调“正常感受力”这一客观标准。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧：
在处理 Nuisance（妨害）问题时，警惕那些基于原告特殊情况（如生病、年老、需要极度安静）的选项。

记住口诀："Objective Standard"（客观标准）。如果一个普通邻居不会觉得这是个大问题，那么这就不是 Nuisance，无论原告多么痛苦。

questions.question:
A buyer bought a large, nicely kept house near a university campus. She was able to buy the house for a very good price because it was located directly across the street from a fraternity house known for its frequent late-night parties. The buyer knew of the fraternity's reputation before she bought the house.
The reputation was well deserved, and the buyer found the noise from the parties extremely unpleasant and disruptive.
The buyer has asked an attorney for legal advice regarding a possible nuisance claim against the fraternity.
Which of the following responses would best express the applicable law?

choices.a: "You have no nuisance claim, because the fraternity members have the right to use their property as they please."
choices.b: "You have no nuisance claim, because you came to the nuisance."
choices.c: "You might have a nuisance claim, but the fact that you bought the house fully aware of the fraternity's habitual late-night activities will count against your claim and could help defeat it."
choices.d: "You will be able to recover damages in a nuisance action, because the late-night activities of the fraternity members violate your right to the quiet enjoyment of your property."

data.questionStem:
Q83825 A buyer bought a large, nicely kept house near a university campus. She was able to buy the house for a very good price because it was located directly across the street from a fraternity house known for its frequent late-night parties. The buyer knew of the fraternity's reputation before she bought the house.

The reputation was well deserved, and the buyer found the noise from the parties extremely unpleasant and disruptive.

The buyer has asked an attorney for legal advice regarding a possible nuisance claim against the fraternity.

Which of the following responses would best express the applicable law? 一名买家在大学校园附近购买了一栋保养良好、面积宽敞的住宅。她能以非常优惠的价格买下这栋房子，因为它正对着一个以频繁举办深夜派对而闻名的兄弟会会所。买家在购房前便知晓该兄弟会的名声。

该兄弟会的名声名副其实，买家发现派对的噪音极其令人不快且具有干扰性。

买家已就可能对该兄弟会提出的妨害索赔向律师寻求法律意见。

下列哪项回应最能表达适用的法律？
options:
A. "You have no nuisance claim, because the fraternity members have the right to use their property as they please."
“您没有妨害索赔权，因为兄弟会成员有权随心所欲地使用其财产。”

B. "You have no nuisance claim, because you came to the nuisance."
“您没有妨害索赔权，因为您属于‘自愿接近妨害’（came to the nuisance）。”

C. "You might have a nuisance claim, but the fact that you bought the house fully aware of the fraternity's habitual late-night activities will count against your claim and could help defeat it."
“您或许拥有妨害索赔权，但您在完全知晓兄弟会习惯性深夜活动的情况下购买该房产这一事实，将对您的索赔不利，并可能导致其败诉。”

D. "You will be able to recover damages in a nuisance action, because the late-night activities of the fraternity members violate your right to the quiet enjoyment of your property."
“您将能够通过妨害诉讼获得损害赔偿，因为兄弟会成员的深夜活动侵犯了您对财产的安宁享有权。”
data.explanation:
Liability for private nuisance arises when the defendant's interference with the plaintiff's use and enjoyment of his/her property was both:
substantial – offensive, annoying, or intolerable to a normal person in the community and
unreasonable – the severity of the plaintiff's harm outweighs the utility of the defendant's conduct.
But if the plaintiff came to the nuisance (ie, acquired or improved property next to a known nuisance), then the court will consider this factor in determining whether the nuisance is actionable (ie, whether the plaintiff can recover for the nuisance).
Here, the buyer might have a private nuisance claim since the fraternity's late-night parties were extremely unpleasant and disruptive to her at home (substantial and unreasonable interference). But since she bought her home knowing the fraternity's reputation for late-night parties (ie, she came to the nuisance), this fact will count against her claim and could help defeat it.
(Choice A) Landowners have the right to use their property in any reasonable way—not in any way they please. Therefore, the buyer could prevail on her nuisance claim if the fraternity's activities were unreasonable and substantially interfered with the use and enjoyment of her home.
(Choice B) The fact that the buyer came to the nuisance is a factor in determining whether the nuisance is actionable but does not bar her claim.
(Choice D) Even if the fraternity's activities violate the buyer's right to enjoy her property, the fact that she knew the fraternity's reputation (ie, she came to the nuisance) could help defeat her claim.
Educational objective:
Coming to the nuisance—ie, acquiring or improving property next to a known nuisance—does not bar a nuisance claim. However, the court will consider this factor in determining whether the plaintiff can recover.



私人妨害责任的产生，须当被告对原告使用和享用其财产的干涉同时满足以下两个条件：
实质性——对社区中的普通人而言是冒犯性的、令人烦恼的或无法忍受的并且
不合理——原告所受损害的严重性超过了被告行为的功用性。
但如果原告自愿接近妨害（即，在已知的妨害源旁购置或改善财产），那么法院在确定该妨害是否可诉（即，原告是否能因此获得赔偿）时，会考量此因素。
在本案中，买家可能拥有私人妨害索赔权，因为兄弟会的深夜派对对她在家的生活造成了极其不快和干扰（实质性且不合理的干涉）。但由于她是在知晓兄弟会深夜派对名声的情况下购买房屋的（即，她自愿接近妨害），这一事实将对她的索赔不利，并可能导致其败诉。
(选项 A) 土地所有者有权以任何合理的方式使用其财产，而非随心所欲。因此，如果兄弟会的活动是不合理的，并对买家使用和享用其住宅构成了实质性干涉，那么买家便可能在妨害索赔中胜诉。
(选项 B) 买家自愿接近妨害这一事实，是确定该妨害是否可诉的一个因素，但并不会直接阻断其索赔权。
(选项 D) 即使兄弟会的活动侵犯了买家享用其财产的权利，她知晓兄弟会名声这一事实（即，她自愿接近妨害）也可能导致其索赔败诉。
教学目标：
自愿接近妨害——即在已知的妨害源旁购置或改善财产——并不会阻断妨害索赔。然而，法院在确定原告是否能获得赔偿时，会考量此因素。

References

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 821D (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (private nuisance).

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 840D (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (coming to the nuisance).

MBE 考点解析

Torts: Private Nuisance
⚖️ 私人妨害 Private Nuisance

定义：对原告使用和享用其土地的权利造成了实质性 (Substantial) 且不合理 (Unreasonable) 的干扰。

本题核心考点

自愿接近妨害 (Coming to the Nuisance)

当原告在购买土地时，已经知道附近存在妨害源（如本题中的兄弟会派对），这在法律上如何认定？

📜 现代法律规则 (Restatement of Torts):

“自愿接近妨害”不是绝对的抗辩理由 (Not a complete bar)，但它是法院在权衡妨害是否“不合理”时必须考虑的一个重要因素。

选项深度解析

选项 C (正确)

法律依据： 选项 C 准确地反映了现代规则。买家知情购房这一事实（Coming to the nuisance）虽然不会直接剥夺她的起诉权，但会作为权衡因素，大大削弱她的胜诉几率。

法院会认为：既然你利用了因噪音而降低的房价（"very good price"），现在反过来要求停止噪音，这可能是不公平的。

选项 A (错误)

理由： 财产权不是绝对的。土地所有者只能以合理 (Reasonable) 的方式使用土地，不能随心所欲地干扰邻居。

选项 B (错误)

理由： 这是旧的普通法规则。在现代法律下，"Coming to the nuisance" 不再是绝对的阻却事由 (Complete defense)，只是考量因素之一。

选项 D (错误)

理由： 过于绝对。虽然噪音干扰了安宁，但法院必须进行利益衡量 (Balancing test)。买家知情且低价购房的事实很可能导致法院判定该干扰在特定情境下并非“不合理”，从而导致她败诉。

💡 MBE 考试通关秘籍

在处理 Nuisance 题目时，请注意区分：

  • Public Nuisance vs. Private Nuisance。
  • 绝对规则 vs. 权衡因素。现代侵权法倾向于使用“合理性权衡” (Reasonableness balancing test)。

看到 "Coming to the nuisance" 时，不要选“直接败诉”或“完全无关”，要选“这是一个会影响结果的考量因素”。

questions.question:
An associate professor in the pediatrics department of a local medical school was denied tenure. He asked a national education lobbying organization to represent him in his efforts to have the tenure decision reversed. In response to a letter from the organization on the professor's behalf, the dean of the medical school wrote to the organization explaining truthfully that the professor had been denied tenure because of reports that he had abused two of his former patients. Several months later, after a thorough investigation, the allegations were proven false, and the professor was granted tenure. He had remained working at the medical school at full pay during the tenure decision review process and thus suffered no pecuniary harm.
In a suit for libel by the professor against the dean of the medical school, will the professor be likely to prevail?

choices.a: No, because the professor invited the libel.
choices.b: No, because the professor suffered no pecuniary loss.
choices.c: Yes, because the dean had a duty to investigate the rumor before repeating it.
choices.d: Yes, because the dean's defamatory statement was in the form of a writing.

data.questionStem:
Q83186

An associate professor in the pediatrics department of a local medical school was denied tenure. He asked a national education lobbying organization to represent him in his efforts to have the tenure decision reversed. In response to a letter from the organization on the professor's behalf, the dean of the medical school wrote to the organization explaining truthfully that the professor had been denied tenure because of reports that he had abused two of his former patients. Several months later, after a thorough investigation, the allegations were proven false, and the professor was granted tenure. He had remained working at the medical school at full pay during the tenure decision review process and thus suffered no pecuniary harm.

In a suit for libel by the professor against the dean of the medical school, will the professor be likely to prevail?

某地医学院儿科系的一位副教授被拒绝授予终身教职。他请求一个全国性的教育游说组织代表他，以推翻该终身教职的决定。医学院院长在回复该组织代表教授发出的信函时，向该组织解释称，该教授之所以被拒绝授予终身教职，是因为有报告称他曾虐待过两名以前的病人。几个月后，经过彻底调查，这些指控被证实是虚假的，该教授获得了终身教职。在终身教职决定的审查过程中，他一直在医学院全薪工作，因此没有遭受金钱上的损害。

在该教授对医学院院长提起的书面诽谤 (libel) 诉讼中，该教授是否可能胜诉？
options:
A. No, because the professor invited the libel.
不会，因为教授招致了该书面诽谤。

B. No, because the professor suffered no pecuniary loss.
不会，因为教授没有遭受金钱损失。

C. Yes, because the dean had a duty to investigate the rumor before repeating it.
会，因为院长在重复该谣言前有义务进行调查。

D. Yes, because the dean's defamatory statement was in the form of a writing.
会，因为院长的诽谤性陈述是以书面形式作出的。
data.explanation:
Libel is a defamatory statement that appears in written or other physical form. To prevail in a suit for libel, the plaintiff must prove all of the following:
  • The defendant knowingly made a false statement about the plaintiff or negligently failed to determine its falsity.
  • That type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation.
  • The defendant intentionally or negligently communicated that statement to a third party (the key to a defamation claim).
However, consent (apparent, actual, or implied) is a complete defense to defamation. Apparent consent exists when the plaintiff's words or conduct were reasonably understood by the defendant as consent to the defamatory communication.

Here, the dean's written response to the organization may have been libelous since it contained false allegations that the professor had abused patients. But since the professor had authorized the organization to investigate his case, it was reasonable for the dean to understand that the professor had invited a response to the organization's inquiry (apparent consent). Therefore, the dean has a valid defense and the professor's claim will likely fail.

(Choice B) Although pecuniary loss is an element of slander (spoken defamation), it is not required for libel (written defamation) since harm is presumed. Therefore, the fact that the professor suffered no pecuniary loss would not defeat his libel claim.

(Choice C) Even if the dean had a duty to investigate the rumor before repeating it (and breached that duty by negligently failing to determine its falsity), the professor will not prevail because the dean has a valid defense to libel (apparent consent).

(Choice D) Although the dean's defamatory statement appeared in physical form (libel) as a written response to the organization's inquiry, the professor will not prevail because he gave the dean apparent consent to respond to that inquiry.

Educational objective: Apparent consent is a defense to defamation when the plaintiff's words or conduct were reasonably understood by the defendant to indicate consent to the defamatory communication.



选项正确率统计：A选项 40%（正确选项），B选项 36%，C选项 11%，D选项 11%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

书面诽谤 (Libel) 是一种以书面或其他有形形式出现的诽谤性陈述。要在书面诽谤 (libel) 诉讼中胜诉，原告必须证明以下所有内容：
  • 被告明知故犯地对原告作出虚假陈述，或因过失未能确定其真伪。
  • 该类型的陈述会损害原告的声誉。
  • 被告故意或因过失将该陈述传达给第三方（诽谤诉讼的关键）。
然而，同意（表见同意、实际同意或默示同意）是诽谤的完全抗辩理由。当原告的言语或行为被被告合理地理解为同意作出该诽谤性通讯时，即构成表见同意 (Apparent consent)。

在本案中，院长对该组织的书面回复可能构成书面诽谤，因为它包含了教授虐待病人的虚假指控。但由于教授已授权该组织调查其案件，院长有理由认为教授已引致其对该组织的询问作出回应（表见同意）。因此，院长拥有有效的抗辩理由，教授的诉讼请求很可能会失败。

（选项 B）尽管金钱损失是口头诽谤 (slander) 的一个要素，但对于书面诽谤 (libel) 而言并非必需，因为损害是被推定的。因此，教授没有遭受金钱损失这一事实不会使其书面诽谤的诉讼请求失败。

（选项 C）即使院长有义务在重复该谣言前进行调查（并且因过失未能确定其真伪而违反了该义务），教授也不会胜诉，因为院长对书面诽谤 (libel) 拥有有效的抗辩理由（表见同意）。

（选项 D）尽管院长的诽谤性陈述以有形形式（书面诽谤）作为对该组织询问的书面回复出现，但教授不会胜诉，因为他给予了院长表见同意来回应此项询问。

教学目标：当原告的言语或行为被被告合理地理解为表示同意作出该诽谤性通讯时，表见同意 (apparent consent) 即构成对诽谤的抗辩理由。

References

  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 558 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (elements of defamation).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 568 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (libel and slander distinguished).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 583 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (consent as a defense to defamation).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考题解析

侵权法 (Torts) - 诽谤 (Defamation)
正确答案
选项 A
No, because the professor invited the libel.
(不会，因为教授招致了该书面诽谤。)
⚖️ 核心考点：同意 (Consent)
本题考察的是诽谤诉讼中的一个绝对抗辩理由：同意 (Consent)。

在侵权法中，如果原告同意被告实施某种行为，那么该行为就不构成侵权。这体现了法谚 Volenti non fit injuria（自愿者不被视为受损）。
🔍 深度解析
关键规则：引致诽谤 (Invited Libel)
当原告或其授权代理人（Agent）主动要求被告解释某些负面决定的原因时，如果被告在回应中诚实地陈述了该原因（即使该原因本身基于虚假谣言），原告被视为对该“发表”行为给予了同意 (Consent)。
本案逻辑推演：
  • 代理关系：教授聘请了游说组织代表他行事。该组织是教授的代理人 (Agent)。
  • 诱发回应：该组织致信医学院院长，实际上是在代表教授询问：“为什么拒绝授予终身教职？”
  • 院长的回应：院长向该组织解释了拒绝的理由（即关于虐待病人的报告）。注意，题目强调院长解释得很诚实 (truthfully)——即他诚实地说明了“拒绝的原因是那份报告”，而不是恶意编造。
  • 结论：由于是教授（通过其代理人）主动引致了这次沟通，这构成了表见同意 (Apparent Consent)。同意是诽谤诉讼的完全抗辩理由 (Complete Defense)。
❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 B 错误
虽然口头诽谤 (Slander) 通常需要证明特殊损害（金钱损失），除非属于本身诽谤 (Slander Per Se)。但本案是书面诽谤 (Libel)，损害通常是被推定的 (Presumed Damages)，不需要证明实际金钱损失。
选项 C 错误
虽然通常被告有义务核实真相，但在存在同意 (Consent) 这一抗辩理由的情况下，被告是否有过失（Negligence）已经不重要了。同意可以阻却违法性。
选项 D 错误
这只是陈述了书面诽谤的形式要件，但忽略了被告拥有的决定性抗辩理由（同意）。
💡 MBE 考试技巧
遇到诽谤题目时，请按以下顺序检查：
  1. 是否构成诽谤的要素（陈述、虚假、发表、损害等）？
  2. 是否存在抗辩事由 (Defenses)？
    • 同意 (Consent)：原告是否通过自己或代理人诱导了该陈述？（本题考点）
    • 真相 (Truth)：陈述是否属实？
    • 特权 (Privilege)：绝对特权或限定特权？
如果存在“同意”，通常直接导致原告败诉，无需再分析过失或损害。
MBE Torts Review | © 2025 Exam Prep

questions.question:
A 15-year-old boy was killed during a gang fight. Two days after his funeral, the boy's mother saw a television program about gang violence and was shocked to see video of herself weeping over the boy's body. The video had been shot by the television reporting team while the boy's body was still lying on a public street. The mother suffered severe emotional distress as a result of seeing the video.
If the mother sues the television station for invasion of her privacy and that of her son, will the mother be likely to prevail?

choices.a: No, because a person has no right to privacy after his or her death.
choices.b: No, because the street was open to the public and the subject was newsworthy.
choices.c: Yes, because the mother did not give permission to have the video used in the program.
choices.d: Yes, because the mother suffered severe emotional distress as a result of viewing the video.

data.questionStem:
Q83805 A 15-year-old boy was killed during a gang fight. Two days after his funeral, the boy's mother saw a television program about gang violence and was shocked to see video of herself weeping over the boy's body. The video had been shot by the television reporting team while the boy's body was still lying on a public street. The mother suffered severe emotional distress as a result of seeing the video.

If the mother sues the television station for invasion of her privacy and that of her son, will the mother be likely to prevail? 一名15岁的男孩在一次帮派斗殴中被杀。在他的葬礼两天后，男孩的母亲看到了一个关于帮派暴力的电视节目，并震惊地发现其中有她俯在男孩尸体上哭泣的视频。该视频是由电视台报道团队在男孩的尸体仍躺在公共街道上时拍摄的。母亲因看到该视频而遭受了严重的精神痛苦。

如果母亲以侵犯她和她儿子的隐私权为由起诉电视台，她是否可能胜诉？
options:
A. No, because a person has no right to privacy after his or her death.
不会，因为一个人在他或她死后没有隐私权。

B. No, because the street was open to the public and the subject was newsworthy.
不会，因为街道是向公众开放的，并且该主题具有新闻价值。

C. Yes, because the mother did not give permission to have the video used in the program.
会，因为母亲没有允许该视频在节目中使用。

D. Yes, because the mother suffered severe emotional distress as a result of viewing the video.
会，因为母亲因观看该视频而遭受了严重的精神痛苦。
data.explanation:
There are four theories of recovery for invasion of privacy:

intrusion upon seclusion – an intentional intrusion (physical or otherwise) on the plaintiff's solitude, seclusion, or private affairs that would be highly offensive to a reasonable person

public disclosure of private facts – publicity given to the plaintiff's private matter (1) that does not address a legitimate public concern, (2) would be highly offensive to a reasonable person and (3) causes damages

appropriation of name or likeness – the unauthorized use of the plaintiff's name, picture, or likeness for a personal benefit (e.g., a monetary advantage)

publicity in a false light – publicity given to false information about the plaintiff with actual malice that places him/her in a false light that would be highly offensive to a reasonable person and causes damages

Here, the woman's invasion of privacy claim will likely fail because the video was taken when the woman and son were on a public street, so it did not intrude upon their private affairs. Additionally, the video was used to present a newsworthy topic and address a legitimate public concern—not for personal benefit or to present false information.

(Choice A) A person has a right to privacy against the appropriation of his/her name or likeness—even after death. But since the television station did not use her son's likeness for personal benefit (e.g., for an advertisement), the mother, suing on her dead son's behalf, will not prevail.

(Choice C) Although the mother did not give the television station permission to use the video in its program, her consent was unnecessary because she was in a public place and the video addressed a newsworthy issue.

(Choice D) Evidence of emotional distress alone is insufficient to prove invasion of privacy. The mother must also show some type of intrusion, publicity, or unauthorized use.

Educational objective: The four theories of recovery for invasion of privacy are: (1) intrusion upon seclusion, (2) appropriation of name or likeness, (3) public disclosure of private facts, and (4) publicity in a false light.

隐私侵权有四种索赔理论：

侵扰个人独处 – 故意（物理或其他方式）侵扰原告的独处、隐居或私事，且该行为对一个通情达理的人来说是极具冒犯性的。

公开披露私密事实 – 公开原告的私事，（1）该事件不涉及正当的公共关注，（2）对一个通情达理的人来说是极具冒犯性的，且（3）造成了损害。

盗用姓名或肖像 – 未经授权使用原告的姓名、照片或肖像以获取个人利益（例如，金钱利益）。

以不实信息歪曲公众形象 – 怀有实际恶意地公开关于原告的虚假信息，将其置于一种对一个通情达理的人来说是极具冒犯性的虚假形象中，并造成了损害。

在此案中，该女士的隐私侵权诉讼很可能会失败，因为视频是在她和她儿子身处公共街道上时拍摄的，因此并未侵扰他们的私事。此外，该视频被用于呈现一个具有新闻价值的话题并涉及正当的公共关注——而不是为了个人利益或呈现虚假信息。

(选项A) 一个人即使在死后，其姓名或肖像仍享有不被盗用的隐私权。但由于电视台并未将其儿子的肖像用于个人利益（例如，用于广告），因此母亲代表她死去的儿子提起的诉讼将不会胜诉。

(选项C) 尽管母亲没有允许电视台在节目中使用该视频，但她的同意是不必要的，因为她当时身处公共场所，且该视频涉及一个具有新闻价值的议题。

(选项D) 仅有精神痛苦的证据不足以证明隐私侵权。母亲还必须证明存在某种类型的侵扰、公开或未经授权的使用。

教学目标： 隐私侵权的四种索赔理论是：（1）侵扰个人独处，（2）盗用姓名或肖像，（3）公开披露私密事实，以及（4）以不实信息歪曲公众形象。

References

Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 652A–652E (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (invasion of privacy).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Invasion of Privacy
(侵权法：隐私权侵权)
核心考点：隐私权的边界

本题考察的是隐私权侵权中的公开披露私密事实 (Public Disclosure of Private Facts)。

要想胜诉，原告必须证明：

  1. 被公开的信息是私密的 (Private)；
  2. 该公开对普通人来说是极具冒犯性的 (Highly Offensive)；
  3. 该信息不属于正当的公众关注 (Not of Legitimate Public Concern)。
本案解析 (正确答案 B)

本案中，母亲无法胜诉，主要基于以下两个关键抗辩理由：

  • 公共场所无隐私 (No Privacy in Public):
    事件发生在公共街道 (Public Street)。法律通常认为，一个人在公共场所的行为没有合理的隐私期待。既然路人都能看到，电视台拍摄并播放就不构成对“私密事实”的披露。
  • 新闻价值抗辩 (Newsworthiness Privilege):
    帮派暴力 (Gang Violence) 是涉及公共利益的话题。根据美国宪法第一修正案对新闻自由的保护，对于具有正当公众关注 (Legitimate Public Concern) 的真实事件的报道，通常享有豁免权，即使这会让当事人感到痛苦。
结论：因为地点公开且话题具有新闻价值，所以不构成侵权。
陷阱选项分析
❌ 选项 A (死后无隐私权):
虽然这是一个普遍原则，但本题中母亲也在起诉侵犯她自己的隐私权。选项A不能解释为什么母亲自己的索赔也会失败。
❌ 选项 C (未获得许可):
考点警示： 在公共场所拍摄具有新闻价值的事件，不需要当事人的同意 (Consent)。只有在用于商业广告（盗用肖像）或侵入私人空间时，同意才至关重要。
❌ 选项 D (精神痛苦):
严重的精神痛苦 (Severe Emotional Distress) 是损害结果，而不是侵权行为成立的前提。如果电视台的行为本身合法（即没有侵犯隐私），无论母亲多么痛苦，都不能因此判定电视台承担隐私侵权责任。
MBE 解题技巧
遇到涉及媒体报道 (Media Publication) 的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：
  1. 地点： 是在公共场所还是私人场所？(Public vs. Private)
  2. 内容： 是具有新闻价值的真实报道，还是商业广告？(News vs. Commercial)

如果是在公共场所拍摄的新闻报道，原告几乎不可能在隐私权诉讼中胜诉。

questions.question:
A man lived in a lakefront home. The man suspected that his neighbor was emptying her septic tank into the lake. Although he did not have any tangible proof, the man had seen the neighbor putting a large hose that led from an area in the neighbor's backyard where the septic tank was located into the lake late at night. Based upon this observation, the man identified the neighbor by name and made the following statement to a local reporter: "She is polluting the lake and ruining its ecosystem by dumping the contents of her septic tank into it every night!"
The reporter published the statement in the newspaper. Upon reading it, the neighbor was horrified because in actuality she had simply been pumping water from the lake into her backyard.
If the neighbor brings a defamation action against the man, will the neighbor be likely to prevail?

choices.a: No, because pollution of the lake is a matter of public concern.
choices.b: No, because the man did not act with actual malice.
choices.c: Yes, because the man acted negligently when he spoke to the reporter about the neighbor.
choices.d: Yes, because the reporter published the man's defamatory statement about the neighbor.

questions.question:
A woman was touring a house that was "for sale by owner." She noticed water stains on the living-room ceiling and asked the seller about them. The seller responded that the roof did not leak even though he knew otherwise. The woman entered into a contract with the seller to purchase the house. The contract had a provision that conditioned the woman's obligation to purchase the house on the receipt of a favorable inspection report by an inspector of her choosing.
The inspection report prepared by the woman's inspector indicated that the roof substantially leaked. However, the woman really wanted the home and purchased it in reliance on the seller's statement regarding the roof's condition. One month later, during the first heavy rain after the purchase, the roof leaked and caused extensive damage to the house.
If the woman sues the seller for fraud, who is likely to prevail?

choices.a: The seller, because the woman did not justifiably rely on the seller's statement that the roof did not leak.
choices.b: The seller, because the woman had a contractual obligation to perform an inspection of the house.
choices.c: The woman, because the roof's condition was a material fact in her decision to purchase the home.
choices.d: The woman, because the seller told her that the roof did not leak even though he knew otherwise.

The seller responded that the roof did not leak even though he knew otherwise. The woman entered into a contract with the seller to purchase the house. The contract had a provision that conditioned the woman's obligation to purchase the house on the receipt of a favorable inspection report by an inspector of her choosing.

The inspection report prepared by the woman's inspector indicated that the roof substantially leaked. However, the woman really wanted the home and purchased it in reliance on the seller's statement regarding the roof's condition. One month later, during the first heavy rain after the purchase, the roof leaked and caused extensive damage to the house.

If the woman sues the seller for fraud, who is likely to prevail?

一名女子正在参观一栋“由业主自售”的房屋。她注意到客厅天花板上有水渍，并向卖方询问。卖方回答说屋顶不漏水，尽管他知道事实并非如此。该女子与卖方签订了购买该房屋的合同。合同中有一项条款，规定女方购买房屋的义务取决于她选择的验房师出具一份令人满意的验房报告。

该女子聘请的验房师准备的验房报告指出，屋顶存在严重漏水。然而，该女子非常想要这栋房子，并信赖卖方关于屋顶状况的陈述而购买了它。一个月后，在购买后的第一场大雨中，屋顶漏水，对房屋造成了广泛的损坏。

如果该女子以欺诈为由起诉卖方，谁可能胜诉？
options:
A. The seller, because the woman did not justifiably rely on the seller's statement that the roof did not leak.
卖方，因为女方对卖方关于屋顶不漏水的陈述没有构成正当信赖。

B. The seller, because the woman had a contractual obligation to perform an inspection of the house.
卖方，因为女方有合同义务对房屋进行检查。

C. The woman, because the roof's condition was a material fact in her decision to purchase the home.
女方，因为屋顶的状况是她决定购买房屋的一个重要事实。

D. The woman, because the seller told her that the roof did not leak even though he knew otherwise.
女方，因为卖方告诉她屋顶不漏水，尽管他知道事实并非如此。
data.explanation:
Misrepresentation


(fraudulent v. negligent)ConductSettingHarm
FraudulentKnowingly or recklessly misrepresented material fact to induce relianceAny settingJustifiable reliance caused pecuniary loss
NegligentNegligently provided plaintiff false informationCommercial setting or setting with risk of physical harmJustifiable reliance caused pecuniary loss or physical harm
A prima facie case of fraud (also called "intentional misrepresentation" or "deceit") is established by proof of the following elements:

  • The defendant knowingly or recklessly misrepresented a material fact with the intent to induce the plaintiff's reliance.
  • The plaintiff justifiably relied on the misrepresentation and suffered pecuniary (ie, financial) loss as a result.


Justifiable reliance does not require the plaintiff to investigate the truth or falsity of the defendant's statement. But reliance is not justifiable if the statement is obviously false OR the defendant is stating a lay opinion.

Here, the seller knowingly misrepresented a material fact when he told the woman that the roof did not leak. The seller presumably intended to induce the woman to purchase the home, and the woman did purchase it in reliance on the seller's statement. But that statement was obviously false in light of the water stains and the report by the woman's own inspector that the roof substantially leaked. Therefore, the woman's reliance was not justifiable and the seller will likely prevail (Choices C & D).

(Choice B) The contract did not obligate the woman to have the house inspected. Instead, it gave her the right to obtain a favorable inspection report before concluding the sale. The woman received an unfavorable report yet chose to rely (unjustifiably) on the seller's statement instead. For this reason, the seller will prevail in the fraud suit.

Educational objective:

Fraud (ie, intentional misrepresentation or deceit) requires proof that the plaintiff's reliance on the defendant's misrepresentation was justifiable. Reliance was not justifiable if the representation was obviously false or the defendant was stating a lay opinion.

选项正确率统计：A选项 62%（正确选项），B选项 7%，C选项 4%，D选项 25%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

虚假陈述


（欺诈性 vs. 过失性）行为场景损害
欺诈性明知或鲁莽地对重要事实作出虚假陈述以引诱信赖任何场景正当信赖导致了金钱损失
过失性过失地向原告提供了虚假信息商业场景或存在身体伤害风险的场景正当信赖导致了金钱损失或身体伤害
欺诈（fraud，亦称“故意虚假陈述”或“deceit”）的初步证据案件（prima facie case）通过证明以下要素而成立：

  • 被告明知或鲁莽地对重要事实作出虚假陈述，意图引诱原告的信赖。
  • 原告正当地信赖了该虚假陈述，并因此遭受了金钱（即财务）损失。


正当信赖不要求原告去调查被告陈述的真伪。但是，如果陈述明显虚假，或者被告陈述的是非专业意见，则该信赖是不正当的。

在本案中，卖方告诉女方屋顶不漏水，这是明知地对一个重要事实作出了虚假陈述。卖方的意图据推测是引诱女方购买该房屋，而女方确实是信赖了卖方的陈述而购买了房屋。但是，鉴于屋顶的水渍以及女方自己的验房师出具的屋顶严重漏水的报告，卖方的陈述明显是虚假的。因此，女方的信赖是不正当的，卖方可能会胜诉（选项 C 和 D 错误）。

（选项 B）合同并未规定女方有义务对房屋进行检查。相反，合同赋予了她在完成交易前获得一份令人满意的验房报告的权利。女方收到了一份不理想的报告，但却选择（不正当地）信赖卖方的陈述。因此，在欺诈诉讼中，卖方将会胜诉。

教学目标：

欺诈（即故意虚假陈述或deceit）要求证明原告对被告虚假陈述的信赖是正当的。如果该陈述明显虚假，或被告陈述的是非专业意见，则该信赖是不正当的。

References

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 525 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (fraudulent misrepresentation).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

侵权法：欺诈与正当信赖
正确答案：选项 A

卖方胜诉，因为女方对卖方关于屋顶不漏水的陈述没有构成正当信赖 (Justifiable Reliance)。

⚖️ 法律规则：欺诈 (Fraud)

在侵权法中，故意虚假陈述 (Intentional Misrepresentation) 或称欺诈 (Deceit/Fraud)，原告必须证明以下所有要素：

  • 虚假陈述 (Misrepresentation)： 被告对重要事实作出了虚假陈述。
  • 明知 (Scienter)： 被告明知陈述虚假或鲁莽地不顾真伪。
  • 意图 (Intent)： 意图引诱原告信赖该陈述。
  • 因果关系 (Causation)： 原告实际上信赖了该陈述。
  • 正当信赖 (Justifiable Reliance)：原告的信赖在客观上必须是合理的。
  • 损害 (Damages)： 造成了实际的金钱损失。
🔍 案情深度解析

本题的核心考点在于“正当信赖” (Justifiable Reliance) 的认定。

1. 卖方确实撒谎了
卖方明知屋顶漏水却说不漏，这满足了“虚假陈述”、“明知”和“意图”的要素。
2. 为什么信赖“不正当”？
虽然女方主观上信赖了卖方的话（她买了房），但法律要求这种信赖必须是Justifiable（正当/合理）的。

在本案中：
  • 女方聘请了验房师。
  • 验房报告明确指出屋顶"substantially leaked" (严重漏水)。

当事实真相（验房报告）已经摆在原告面前，且原告已经知晓该事实与被告的陈述相矛盾时，原告选择无视真相而继续相信谎言，这种信赖在法律上被视为不正当 (Unjustifiable)。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 B (合同义务)
这是干扰项。合同赋予了她检查的权利 (Right)，而非强制义务。即使有义务，本案的关键在于她已经检查了，并且知道了真相，从而切断了欺诈索赔的信赖链条。
选项 C (重要事实)
虽然屋顶状况确实是重要事实 (Material Fact)，但这只是欺诈成立的要素之一。如果缺少“正当信赖”这一要素，即便事实再重要，欺诈指控也无法成立。
选项 D (卖方撒谎)
这是很多考生的错选点。虽然卖方道德上有亏（明知故犯），但在普通法下的欺诈诉讼中，原告不能“闭目塞听”。如果原告已经通过调查发现了真相，就不能再声称自己被欺骗了。
💡 MBE 备考锦囊

警惕“显然虚假”的情况：

在 MBE 欺诈题中，如果被告的谎言是显而易见 (Obviously false) 的，或者原告已经通过自己的调查发现了真相，那么原告的信赖就永远不是“正当”的。此时，无论被告多么恶意，欺诈诉讼通常都会失败。

questions.question:
The governor of State A signed a death warrant for a convicted murderer. At a demonstration protesting the execution of the murderer, two opponents of the death penalty carried large signs that stated, "The governor is a murderer!" A television station broadcasted news coverage of the demonstration, including pictures of the signs carried by the two protestors. The broadcast caused the governor severe emotional distress.
If the governor asserts a defamation claim against the television station, will he prevail?

choices.a: No, if the only reasonable interpretation of the signs was that the term "murderer" was intended as a characterization of one who would sign a death warrant.
choices.b: No, unless the governor proves he suffered pecuniary loss resulting from harm to his reputation proximately caused by the protestors' signs.
choices.c: Yes, because the signs would cause persons to hold the governor in lower esteem.
choices.d: Yes, if the governor proves that the television station showed the signs with knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard of the truth that the governor had not committed homicide.

data.questionStem:
Q83153

The governor of State A signed a death warrant for a convicted murderer. At a demonstration protesting the execution of the murderer, two opponents of the death penalty carried large signs that stated, "The governor is a murderer!" A television station broadcasted news coverage of the demonstration, including pictures of the signs carried by the two protestors. The broadcast caused the governor severe emotional distress.

If the governor asserts a defamation claim against the television station, will he prevail?

A州州长为一名已定罪的杀人犯签署了死刑执行令。在一场抗议对该杀人犯执行死刑的示威活动中，两名死刑反对者举着大标语，上面写着：“州长是杀人犯！”一家电视台播报了这场示威活动的新闻，其中包括两名抗议者所持标语的画面。该广播给州长造成了严重的精神痛苦。

如果州长对该电视台提起诽谤诉讼，他会胜诉吗？
options:
A. No, if the only reasonable interpretation of the signs was that the term "murderer" was intended as a characterization of one who would sign a death warrant.
不会，如果对标语的唯一合理解释是，“杀人犯”一词意在描述签署死刑执行令之人的品性。

B. No, unless the governor proves he suffered pecuniary loss resulting from harm to his reputation proximately caused by the protestors' signs.
不会，除非州长证明他因抗议者标语近因导致的声誉损害而遭受了金钱损失。

C. Yes, because the signs would cause persons to hold the governor in lower esteem.
会，因为这些标语会导致他人对州长的评价降低。

D. Yes, if the governor proves that the television station showed the signs with knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard of the truth that the governor had not committed homicide.
会，如果州长证明电视台在播放这些标语时，明知州长没有犯下杀人罪这一事实为虚假，或鲁莽地漠视其真实性。
data.explanation:
Defamatory statements Statements that would tend to harm plaintiff's reputation by either: lowering plaintiff's standing in community (eg, allegations challenging plaintiff's integrity or financial reputation) or deterring third parties from associating or dealing with plaintiff (eg, allegations that plaintiff is insane or diseased) Defamation can be either slander (spoken statements) OR libel (statements made in physical form or that appear on radio or television - as seen here). When a defamation claim based on libel is brought by a public official or public figure, he/she must prove all of the following:
  • The defendant made a false statement about the plaintiff with actual malice - knowledge or reckless disregard of the statement's falsity.
  • That type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation.
  • The defendant intentionally or negligently communicated that statement to a third party.
A statement would only tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation if a third party's reasonable interpretation of that statement would tend to do so. Here, the television station broadcasted pictures of protestors' signs that stated, "The governor is a murderer!" But those signs would not tend to harm the governor's reputation if they could only be reasonably interpreted to mean that a person who signs a death warrant should be characterized as a murderer - not that the governor actually committed murder. In that case, the governor's defamation claim would fail.

(Choice B) Libel does not require proof of pecuniary loss (ie, financial harm). Instead, the governor's claim would fail if a reasonable interpretation of the protestors' signs would not harm his reputation.

(Choice C) Even if the signs would cause persons to hold the governor in lower esteem (ie, harm his reputation), the governor (public official) can only prevail if he also proves that the television station acted with actual malice.

(Choice D) Assuming that the governor proves that the television station knew that the signs were false or recklessly disregarded their falsity (actual malice), he would still have to prove that a third party's reasonable interpretation of those signs would tend to harm his reputation.

Educational objective: A plaintiff can only recover for libel (defamation in physical form or that appears on radio or television) if a third party's reasonable interpretation of the defendant's statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation.

选项正确率统计：A选项 56%（正确选项），B选项 10%，C选项 0%，D选项 31%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

诽谤性陈述 指通过以下任一方式可能损害原告声誉的陈述：降低原告在社区中的地位（例如，挑战原告正直或财务声誉的指控）或阻止第三方与原告交往或交易（例如，指控原告精神失常或患有疾病）。诽谤可以是口头诽谤（slander，即口头陈述）或书面诽谤（libel，即以物理形式作出或出现在广播或电视上的陈述——如此处所示）。当公职人员或公众人物提起基于书面诽谤（libel）的诽谤诉讼时，他/她必须证明以下所有内容：
  • 被告对原告作出了虚假陈述，且带有真实恶意——即明知其虚假或鲁莽地漠视其真实性。
  • 该类陈述会倾向于损害原告的声誉。
  • 被告故意或过失地将该陈述传播给了第三方。
只有当第三方对陈述的合理解释会倾向于损害原告声誉时，该陈述才构成可能损害原告声誉。在本案中，电视台播报了抗议者标语的画面，标语上写着：“州长是杀人犯！”但是，如果对这些标语的唯一合理解释是，签署死刑执行令的人应被定性为杀人犯——而不是指州长实际犯下了谋杀罪，那么这些标语就不会倾向于损害州长的声誉。在这种情况下，州长的诽谤诉讼将会失败。

（选项B）书面诽谤（Libel）不需要证明金钱损失（即财务损害）。相反，如果对抗议者标语的合理解释不会损害州长的声誉，他的诉讼就会失败。

（选项C）即使标语会导致他人降低对州长的评价（即损害其声誉），州长（作为公职人员）也必须证明电视台具有真实恶意才能胜诉。

（选项D）即使州长证明电视台明知标语虚假或鲁莽地漠视其真实性（即具有真实恶意），他仍需证明第三方对这些标语的合理解释会倾向于损害其声誉。

教学目标：只有当第三方对被告陈述的合理解释会倾向于损害原告声誉时，原告才能因书面诽谤（libel，即以物理形式或在广播电视上出现的诽谤）获得赔偿。

References

  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 558 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (elements of defamation).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 568 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (libel and slander distinguished).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 580A (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (defamation of public official or public figure).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

侵权法 (Torts) - 诽谤 (Defamation)

Topic: Defamatory Meaning
⚖️ 核心法则 (The Rule)

要构成诽谤，陈述必须是事实断言 (Statement of Fact)。纯粹的意见 (Opinion) 或修辞性夸张 (Rhetorical Hyperbole)，如果不能被合理地解释为陈述了实际事实，则不构成诽谤。

🔍 案情深度解析

本案的核心在于如何理解标语“州长是杀人犯 (The governor is a murderer)”：

  • 背景 (Context)： 抗议死刑执行的示威活动。
  • 对象 (Subject)： 签署死刑执行令的州长。
  • 关键问题： 普通人看到这个标语，会认为州长真的触犯了刑法（事实），还是认为这是对抗议者对死刑制度的道德抨击（意见/夸张）？
✅ 为什么选 A？

选项 A 指出了诽谤成立的前提条件缺失。

最高法院在 Greenbelt Coop. Pub. Ass'n v. Bresler 等案件中确立了原则：如果在特定语境下，一个词汇（如“勒索”、“杀人犯”）明显是作为修辞性夸张 (Rhetorical Hyperbole) 使用，且任何理性的读者/听众都不会将其理解为字面意义上的犯罪指控，那么该陈述就不具有诽谤性 (Defamatory)。

在本案中，如果唯一的合理解释是“签署死刑令的人在道德上等同于杀人犯”，那么这就是一种受宪法保护的政治评论，而非事实陈述。因此，州长无法胜诉。

❌ 陷阱排除
选项 B 关于金钱损失 (Pecuniary Loss)
错误。书面诽谤 (Libel) 通常不需要证明特殊损害 (Special Damages/Pecuniary Loss)，损害是被推定的。更重要的是，如果陈述本身不构成诽谤（如本案中的意见表达），是否有损失都无关紧要。
选项 C 关于声誉降低 (Lower Esteem)
错误。虽然诽谤确实需要导致声誉受损，但对于公职人员 (Public Official)，仅有声誉受损是不够的，还必须证明真实恶意 (Actual Malice)。此外，如果陈述被视为“意见”，即使它降低了某人的评价，也不构成诽谤。
选项 D 关于真实恶意 (Actual Malice)
这是一个极具诱惑力的干扰项。虽然公职人员原告必须证明真实恶意（明知虚假或鲁莽漠视真相），但前提是该陈述必须是事实陈述。如果标语被认定为“修辞性夸张”（非事实），那么被告是否知道其“虚假”就变得没有意义了，因为意见无所谓真假。
💡 MBE 提分技巧

在处理涉及第一修正案 (First Amendment) 的诽谤题时，首先判断陈述是事实 (Fact) 还是意见 (Opinion)。如果是政治抗议背景下的激烈言辞（如 traitor, blackmailer, murderer），法院通常倾向于将其视为修辞性夸张，不予追究。

questions.question:
A female quarterback was the only female on an otherwise all-male college football team. During training one day, one of the team's offensive linemen saw the female quarterback hidden behind the bleachers, injecting herself with a needle. The lineman immediately told the football team's coach that he had just seen the female quarterback injecting herself with steroids. The female quarterback was diabetic and had actually been injecting insulin into her arm when the lineman saw her behind the bleachers. However, not knowing this, the coach suspended the female quarterback from the team.
If the female quarterback files a defamation suit against the lineman, who is likely to prevail?

choices.b: The female quarterback, because the statement was false and the lineman was negligent in making it.

厨师的遗产管理人会胜诉吗？
options:
A. No, because the chef is deceased.
不会，因为该厨师已故。

B. No, because there was no publication.

data.explanation:
Defamation can be either libel (written statements) OR slander (spoken statements - as seen here). A plaintiff has an action for defamation based on slander if all of the following elements are met:

  • The defendant knowingly made a false statement about the plaintiff (or negligently failed to determine its falsity).
  • The statement was defamatory, meaning that the type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation.
  • The defendant intentionally or negligently communicated the statement to a third party who understood it.
  • The statement caused the plaintiff special damage (usually monetary loss) or was slanderous per se.


However, defamation of a deceased person is not actionable.† Therefore, the chef's estate will not prevail in a defamation suit against the sous chef.

†A statement about a dead person may amount to defamation of a living person. Additionally, whether an action for defamation of a living person survives the person's death depends on the state's survival statute.

(Choice B) The publication (ie, communication) element for defamation was met when the sous chef intentionally told the restaurant's customers that the chef was a fraud and that a dishwasher had created the recipes.

(Choices C & D) Calling the chef a fraud was harmful to her reputation and may have impacted cookbook sales (special damage). But defamation of a deceased person is not actionable.

Educational objective: A defamation claim based on libel (written statements) or slander (spoken statements) of a deceased person is not actionable.

诽谤 (Defamation) 可分为书面诽谤 (libel)（书面陈述）与口头诽谤 (slander)（口头陈述——如此案所示）。原告可基于口头诽谤 (slander) 提起诉讼，但须满足以下所有要件：

  • 被告故意作出关于原告的虚假陈述（或因过失未能确定其虚假性）。
  • 该陈述具有诽谤性，即该类陈述往往会损害原告的声誉。
  • 被告故意或因过失将该陈述传达给能理解其内容的第三方。
  • 该陈述给原告造成了特殊损害（通常是金钱损失）或构成当然诽谤 (slanderous per se)。


然而，对已故人士的诽谤不具有可诉性 (actionable)。† 因此，厨师的遗产管理人在对副厨师长提起的诽谤诉讼中将不会胜诉。

†关于死者的陈述可能构成对在世之人的诽谤。此外，一项针对在世之人的诽谤诉讼在其死亡后能否存续，取决于州的存续法 (survival statute)。

(选项B) 当副厨师长故意告诉餐厅顾客该厨师是骗子，并且配方是由一名洗碗工创作的时候，诽谤的公开传播 (publication)（即传达）要件已经满足。

(选项C和D) 称该厨师为骗子损害了她的声誉，并可能影响了食谱的销量（特殊损害）。但对已故人士的诽谤不具有可诉性。

教学要点：对已故人士的书面诽谤 (libel) 或口头诽谤 (slander) 不构成可诉的法律主张。

MBE 考点解析

侵权法 (Torts) - 诽谤 (Defamation)

本题考察的是诽谤法中关于原告资格的一个核心原则。正确答案是 A。

核心法律规则 (The Rule) 根据普通法规则，已故人士不能被诽谤。

Defamation of a deceased person is not actionable.

诽谤侵权旨在保护个人的名誉 (Reputation)。法律认为，一旦人去世，其名誉权随之终止。因此，对于死后发表的言论，无论多么恶劣或虚假，死者的遗产管理人 (Estate) 或亲属均无权提起诽谤诉讼。

案情分析 (Analysis)

1. 诽谤的发生时间点：
题目明确指出，副厨师长是在厨师去世后 (After the chef died) 才开始散布谣言的。
2. 法律后果：
虽然副厨师长的言论满足了诽谤的其他构成要件（虚假陈述、公开传播、造成损害），但由于原告（厨师）在言论发表时已经去世，不存在法律上的受害主体。因此，遗产管理人无法胜诉。

为什么排除其他选项？

  • 选项 B (No publication)： 错误。副厨师长将言论告诉了顾客，这已经满足了公开传播 (Publication) 的要件。传播给任何第三方即构成 Publication。
  • 选项 C & D (Damages)： 错误。虽然言论确实损害了名誉并影响了销量（构成了特殊损害 Special Damages），但因为缺少了“在世的原告”这一前提条件，损害再大也无法通过诽谤之诉获得救济。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

区分“死者诽谤”与“诉讼存续”：

在做题时，务必看清诽谤发生的时间：

  1. 死后被骂： 如本题，言论发表于死后 → 不可诉 (Not Actionable)。
  2. 生前被骂，死后起诉： 如果诽谤发生在厨师活着的时候，而她在诉讼过程中去世了，根据大多数州的存续法 (Survival Statutes)，其遗产管理人可以继续进行诉讼。

本题的关键在于言论发表于死者去世之后。

questions.question:
A statistics professor told a friend that one of the professor's graduate students had failed an introductory statistics course in the second quarter of his sophomore year in college. The friend repeated this statement to an economics professor, but the friend prefaced it with the proviso that she had heard the information from the statistics professor and had no personal knowledge of whether it was true.
The student later learned of the statement and initiated a lawsuit against the friend for slander. At trial, the friend offered evidence of the student's college transcript from sophomore year. However, the transcript proved that the student had failed the introductory statistics course in the first quarter, not the second quarter, of his sophomore year in college.
Can the student likely recover?

choices.a: No, because the friend merely repeated what she had heard from the statistics professor.
choices.b: No, because the statement is substantially true.
choices.c: Yes, because the friend was negligent in failing to verify the statement before repeating it.
choices.d: Yes, because the friend's statement was inaccurate.

A man sued his neighbor for defamation based on the following facts: The neighbor told a friend that the man had set fire to a house in the neighborhood. The friend, who knew the man well, did not believe the neighbor's allegation, and the neighbor in fact knew that it was false. The friend told the man about the neighbor's allegation. The man was very upset by the allegation, but neither the man nor the neighbor nor the friend communicated the allegation to anyone else.
Should the man prevail in his lawsuit?

choices.a: No, because the friend did not believe what the neighbor had said.
choices.b: No, because the man cannot prove that he suffered pecuniary loss.
choices.c: Yes, because the man was very upset at hearing what the neighbor had said.
choices.d: Yes, because the neighbor communicated to the friend the false accusation that the man had committed a serious crime.

一名男子以诽谤为由起诉其邻居，案件事实如下：该邻居告诉一位朋友，说该男子在社区里放火烧了一栋房子。这位朋友很了解该男子，因此不相信邻居的指控，而邻居事实上也知道该指控是虚假的。这位朋友将邻居的指控告诉了该男子。该男子对这一指控感到非常不安，但除了该男子、邻居和这位朋友之外，没有人将此指控传达给任何其他人。

该男子能否在此诉讼中胜诉？
options:
A. No, because the friend did not believe what the neighbor had said.
不能，因为那位朋友不相信邻居所说的话。

B. No, because the man cannot prove that he suffered pecuniary loss.
不能，因为该男子无法证明他遭受了金钱损失。

C. Yes, because the man was very upset at hearing what the neighbor had said.
能，因为该男子在听到邻居所说的话后感到非常不安。

D. Yes, because the neighbor communicated to the friend the false accusation that the man had committed a serious crime.
能，因为邻居向那位朋友传达了该男子犯下严重罪行的虚假指控。
data.explanation:
Defamation can be either libel (written statements) OR slander ( spoken statements - as seen here). To establish a defamation claim based on slander, the plaintiff must prove all of the following:
  • The defendant knowingly made a false statement about the plaintiff (or negligently failed to determine its falsity).
  • That type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation.
  • The defendant intentionally or negligently communicated that statement to a third party.
  • That statement caused the plaintiff special damage (ie, pecuniary/monetary loss).
However, some spoken statements are slanderous per se because they are so harmful to the plaintiff's reputation that damages are presumed. Therefore, proof of special damage is unnecessary when a statement falsely accused the plaintiff of any of the following:
  • committing a serious crime (eg, arson, murder, rape, theft)
  • engaging in conduct that adversely affects the plaintiff's occupation (eg, butcher sells rotten meats)
  • committing serious sexual misconduct (eg, adultery)
  • having a loathsome disease (eg, sexually transmitted infection)
Here, the neighbor falsely told the friend that the man had set fire to a house in the neighborhood (serious crime). Since that type of statement constitutes slander per se, the man's harm is presumed. Therefore, the man should prevail in his defamation lawsuit even if he cannot prove pecuniary loss (Choice B).

(Choice A) Defamation requires proof that the defendant's false statement was communicated to a third party - not that the third party believed it. Therefore, the man can prevail even if the friend did not believe the neighbor's allegation.

(Choice C) Defamation does not require proof of emotional distress, so the fact that the man was very upset after hearing the neighbor's allegation has no effect on the viability of the man's claim. However, proof of emotional distress would be required in an intentional or negligent infliction of emotional distress claim.

Educational objective: Slander generally requires proof of special damage. However, damage is presumed when the statement was slanderous per se - ie, it accused the plaintiff of (1) a serious crime, (2) conduct that adversely affects his/her occupation, (3) serious sexual misconduct, or (4) having a loathsome disease.

诽谤 (Defamation) 可以是书面诽谤 (libel)（书面陈述）或口头诽谤 (slander)（口头陈述——如此案所示）。要基于口头诽谤 (slander) 成立诽谤诉请，原告必须证明以下所有要件：
  • 被告明知地对原告做出了虚假陈述（或因过失未能确定其虚假性）。
  • 该类型的陈述会倾向于损害原告的声誉。
  • 被告故意或因过失将该陈述传达给了第三方。
  • 该陈述给原告造成了特殊损害（即金钱/经济损失）。
然而，某些口头陈述本身即构成诽谤 (slanderous per se)，因为它们对原告声誉的损害极为严重，以至于损害赔偿是推定成立的。因此，当一项陈述虚假地指控原告有以下任何一种行为时，无需证明特殊损害：
  • 犯下严重罪行（例如，纵火、谋杀、强奸、盗窃）
  • 从事对其职业产生不利影响的行为（例如，屠夫出售腐烂的肉）
  • 犯有严重的性行为不端（例如，通奸）
  • 患有令人厌恶的疾病（例如，性传播感染）
在本案中，邻居虚假地告诉朋友，该男子在社区放火烧了一栋房子（严重罪行）。由于此类陈述构成本身即诽谤 (slander per se)，该男子的损害是推定成立的。因此，即使该男子无法证明金钱损失，他也应在诽谤诉讼中胜诉（选项B）。

（选项A）诽谤要求证明被告的虚假陈述被传达给了第三方——而不是第三方相信了该陈述。因此，即使那位朋友不相信邻居的指控，该男子也能胜诉。

（选项C）诽谤不要求证明精神痛苦，因此该男子在听到邻居的指控后感到非常不安这一事实，对该男子诉请的可行性没有影响。但是，在“故意或过失施加精神痛苦”的诉请中，则需要证明精神痛苦。

教学目标：口头诽谤 (Slander) 通常需要证明特殊损害。但是，当陈述本身即构成诽谤 (slanderous per se) 时——即指控原告（1）犯有严重罪行，（2）从事对其职业产生不利影响的行为，（3）犯有严重的性行为不端，或（4）患有令人厌恶的疾病——损害赔偿是推定成立的。

References

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 558 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (defamation elements).

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 568 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (libel and slander distinguished).

Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 570 - 74 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (slander per se).

MBE 考点解析

Torts: Defamation (Slander)

正确答案：D

该男子能胜诉，因为邻居向朋友传达了关于该男子犯下严重罪行的虚假指控。

⚖️ 核心法律逻辑解析

本题考察的是诽谤法中关于口头诽谤 (Slander) 和本身诽谤 (Slander Per Se) 的区别。

通常情况下，原告要赢得口头诽谤诉讼，必须证明遭受了特殊损害 (Special Damages)，即具体的金钱或经济损失（Pecuniary Loss）。

但是，本案适用了一个关键的例外规则：

关键规则：本身诽谤 (Slander Per Se)

如果口头诽谤的内容属于以下四类之一，法律推定原告遭受了损害，原告无需证明具体的金钱损失：

  1. 严重罪行 (Serious Crime)：如涉及道德败坏的犯罪（本案中的纵火 Arson）。
  2. 职业不端 (Business/Profession)：影响原告职业能力的指控。
  3. 严重性行为不端 (Serious Sexual Misconduct)：通常指通奸或滥交。
  4. 令人厌恶的疾病 (Loathsome Disease)：如性病或麻风病。

本案应用：
邻居指控该男子“放火烧房子”（纵火），这属于严重罪行。因此，这构成了 Slander Per Se。损害被法律推定存在，该男子无需像选项 B 所说的那样证明金钱损失。

🚫 排除干扰项 (MBE 陷阱)
关于“第三方是否相信” (选项 A)：
诽谤的构成要件之一是发布 (Publication)，即向第三方传达。只要第三方听到了并理解了该陈述，发布就完成了。至于第三方是否相信该指控，只影响损害赔偿的数额，而不影响侵权责任的成立。
关于“精神痛苦” (选项 C)：
虽然该男子感到不安，但诽谤法的核心是保护声誉 (Reputation)，而非情绪。虽然精神痛苦可以作为附带损害赔偿，但它不是胜诉的理由。胜诉的理由是“本身诽谤”的性质。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)：
在 MBE 诽谤题目中，首先判断是 Libel（书面，通常无需证明特殊损害）还是 Slander（口头）。如果是 Slander，立即检查是否落入上述 4 类 Per Se 类别。如果是，直接排除“需要证明金钱损失”的选项。

questions.question:
A man lives in a small community where there is only one judge. The man recently lost a highly publicized court case that had been adjudicated by her, and he was convinced that she had issued an unfair judgment. As the man left the courthouse, he made this statement to a reporter: "Judges are crooks, and they will accept bribes if you pay them enough!" The statement was subsequently printed in the local newspaper.
The judge had never accepted a bribe, and after reading the statement in the newspaper, she filed a defamation action against the man.
Will the judge be likely to prevail?

choices.a: No, because the defamatory language applied to judges in general.
choices.b: No, because the man's statement did not cause the judge actual harm.
choices.c: Yes, because a reasonable person would conclude that the man's statement referred to the judge.
choices.d: Yes, because the statement was published in the local newspaper.

One day, the manager accused the employee, in Spanish and in front of other employees, of stealing a valuable item from the manager's office. Shortly after making this accusation, the manager discovered that she had accidently failed to see the item on her desk and apologized to the employee.
The employee sued the manager for defamation.
Is the employee likely to prevail in his suit?

choices.a: No, because none of the other employees understood Spanish.
choices.b: No, because the manager mistakenly believed that the employee stole the item.
choices.c: Yes, because the manager made the defamatory statement in front of other employees.
choices.d: Yes, because the manager's accusation amounted to slander per se.

data.explanation:
Defamation can be either libel (written statements) OR slander ( spoken statements - as seen here). For defamation based on slander, the plaintiff must prove that:
  • the defendant knowingly made a false statement about the plaintiff OR negligently failed to determine its falsity
  • that type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation
  • the defendant intentionally or negligently communicated (ie, published) that statement to a third party who understood the statement's message and
  • that statement caused the plaintiff special damage (monetary loss) OR constituted slander per se (eg, accused the plaintiff of theft or other serious crime).


Here, the manager falsely stated that the employee stole a valuable item from her office in front of other employees. But since that statement was made in Spanish, none of the other employees understood. Therefore, the employee will likely not prevail on his defamation claim (Choice C).

(Choice B) A plaintiff who is a public figure or official must prove that the defendant made the defamatory statement with actual malice - ie, knowledge or reckless disregard of the statement's falsity. But since the employee is a private individual, he need only prove that the manager negligently failed to determine falsity.

(Choice D) Although the manager's accusation that the employee committed theft (a serious crime) constituted slander per se, the employee will not prevail because none of the other employees understood the accusation.

Educational objective: Defamation requires proof that the defendant intentionally or negligently communicated a false statement about the plaintiff to a third party who understood its meaning.



选项正确率统计：A选项 82%（正确选项），B选项 6%，C选项 6%，D选项 4%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

诽谤 (Defamation) 可以是书面诽谤 (libel)（书面陈述）或口头诽谤 (slander)（口头陈述——如此处所示）。对于基于口头诽谤的诽谤诉讼，原告必须证明：
  • 被告明知有关原告的陈述是虚假的，或因过失未能确定其虚假性
  • 该类陈述会损害原告的声誉
  • 被告故意或因过失将该陈述传达（即发表）给了一个能够理解该陈述含义的第三方，并且
  • 该陈述给原告造成了特殊损害（金钱损失），或构成了本身即是诽谤（slander per se）（例如，指控原告盗窃或其他严重犯罪）。


在本案中，经理在其他员工面前虚假地陈述该员工从她办公室偷走了一件贵重物品。但由于该陈述是用西班牙语做出的，没有其他员工听懂。因此，该员工的诽谤诉讼请求很可能不会成功（选项C）。

（选项B） 作为公众人物或官员的原告必须证明被告做出诽谤性陈述时带有“真实恶意”（actual malice）——即明知其虚假或鲁莽地（reckless）罔顾其真伪。但由于该员工是普通个人，他只需证明经理因过失未能确定其虚假性。

（选项D） 尽管经理指控员工犯有盗窃罪（一种严重犯罪）构成了本身即是诽谤（slander per se），但由于没有其他员工听懂这一指控，该员工仍不会胜诉。

教学目标：诽谤 (Defamation) 要求证明被告故意或因过失将关于原告的虚假陈述传达给了能够理解其含义的第三方。

References

  • Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 558 - 59, 568, 570, 577, 580B (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (elements of defamation).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 570 - 74 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (slander per se).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 577 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (communication/publication requirement).

MBE 考点解析

侵权法：诽谤与发表要素

正确答案
选项 A
不会胜诉，因为没有其他员工听得懂西班牙语。
核心法律规则解析
发表 (Publication) 的定义

在诽谤法（Defamation）中，原告必须证明被告将诽谤性言论“发表”给了第三方。这里的“发表”不仅仅是说出来，还要求：

  • 被告有意或过失地将言论传达给第三方；并且
  • 第三方必须理解（Understand）该言论的含义。

根据 Restatement (Second) of Torts § 577，如果第三方因为听不懂所使用的语言（Foreign Language）而无法理解诽谤性陈述的内容，那么这就不构成法律意义上的“发表”。

本案分析：
经理虽然当着其他员工的面指控了该员工（Slander），但她使用的是西班牙语。题目明确指出“没有其他员工会说或听懂西班牙语”。因此，对于在场的第三方来说，这些话只是无意义的声音，他们并没有接收到“该员工是小偷”这一诽谤性信息。由于缺乏有效的“发表”，诽谤诉讼无法成立。

为什么其他选项是陷阱？
陷阱：本身即是诽谤 (Slander Per Se)

选项 D 是最具迷惑性的干扰项。

确实，指控他人犯有严重犯罪（如盗窃）通常属于 Slander Per Se，这意味着原告不需要证明具体的金钱损失（Special Damages）。

但是！ Slander Per Se 只是免除了证明损害的责任，它并不能免除证明诽谤基本要素（如发表）的责任。如果连最基本的“发表”都没有发生，那么言论的内容是否恶劣就无关紧要了。

选项 B (错误认为)：
虽然经理确实弄错了（Negligence），但在诽谤法中，被告的过失是关于言论真实性的。即使被告有过失，如果言论没有被第三方理解（即未发表），侵权行为仍未完成。

选项 C (当众陈述)：
仅仅“在他人面前”说话是不够的，关键在于他人是否理解。如果经理是用英语说的，那么选项 C 就会成立。

MBE 解题技巧：
看到“外语”、“方言”或“噪音太大听不见”的情节时，
立即检查“发表 (Publication)”这一要素是否缺失。

questions.question:
A newspaper printed an article that stated: "The popular restaurant on the town square has closed its doors. The restaurant's employees have said that the closing resulted from the owner's belief that the restaurant's general manager has embezzled thousands of dollars from the restaurant over the last several years. A decision on reopening the restaurant will be made after the completion of an audit of the restaurant's books."
The restaurant's general manager brought a libel action against the newspaper based on the publication of this article. The parties stipulated that the general manager never embezzled any funds from the restaurant.
The case went to trial before a jury. The newspaper filed a motion for a directed verdict at the close of the evidence.
Why should the court grant the motion?

choices.a: The evidence is not clear and convincing that the newspaper published the article with "actual malice."
choices.b: The record contains no evidence that the general manager suffered special harm as a result of the publication.
choices.c: The record contains no evidence that the newspaper was negligent as to the truth or falsity of the charge of embezzlement.
choices.d: The record contains uncontradicted evidence that the article accurately reported what the employees told the newspaper.

Q83154

The restaurant's employees have said that the closing resulted from the owner's belief that the restaurant's general manager has embezzled thousands of dollars from the restaurant over the last several years. A decision on reopening the restaurant will be made after the completion of an audit of the restaurant's books."

The restaurant's general manager brought a libel action against the newspaper based on the publication of this article. The parties stipulated that the general manager never embezzled any funds from the restaurant.

The case went to trial before a jury. The newspaper filed a motion for a directed verdict at the close of the evidence.

Why should the court grant the motion?

一家报纸刊登了一篇文章，内容如下：“镇上广场那家受欢迎的餐厅已经关门。该餐厅的员工称，关门是因为店主认为餐厅的总经理在过去几年里侵吞了数千美元。餐厅是否重新开业，将在完成账目审计后决定。”

该餐厅的总经理基于这篇文章的发表，对该报纸提起了诽谤诉讼。双方当事人约定，该总经理从未侵吞过餐厅的任何资金。

案件进入陪审团审理阶段。在证据出示结束时，该报纸提出了一项要求指示裁决的动议。

法院为何应当批准该动议？
options:
A. The evidence is not clear and convincing that the newspaper published the article with "actual malice."
没有明确且有说服力的证据表明，该报纸是以“实际恶意”发表该文章的。

B. The record contains no evidence that the general manager suffered special harm as a result of the publication.
案卷中没有证据表明，该总经理因文章的发表而遭受了特殊损害。

C. The record contains no evidence that the newspaper was negligent as to the truth or falsity of the charge of embezzlement.
案卷中没有证据表明，该报纸对于侵吞指控的真伪存在过失。

D. The record contains uncontradicted evidence that the article accurately reported what the employees told the newspaper.
案卷中有无可辩驳的证据表明，该文章准确报道了员工告知报纸的内容。
data.explanation:
Libel is defamation that appears in written or other physical form. To prevail in a suit for libel, the plaintiff must prove all of the following:

  • The defendant knowingly made a false statement about the plaintiff OR negligently failed to determine its falsity (ie, failed to use reasonable care).
  • That type of statement would tend to harm the plaintiff's reputation.
  • The defendant intentionally or negligently communicated that statement to a third party.


If the plaintiff fails to present legally sufficient evidence to support all of these elements at trial (ie, no reasonable jury could find in the plaintiff's favor), the court should grant the defendant's motion for a directed verdict.

Here, the newspaper falsely reported that the general manager had embezzled thousands of dollars in a published article. But there is no evidence that the newspaper knew or negligently failed to determine that the embezzlement charge was false since it used reasonable care by consulting with former restaurant employees about that charge. As a result, the court should grant the newspaper's motion for a directed verdict.

(Choice A) A libel claim brought by a public figure or official (eg, celebrity, politician) requires clear and convincing evidence that the defendant made a statement with actual malice - knowledge or reckless disregard of the statement's falsity. But a claim brought by a private person (eg, the general manager) only requires proof by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant knew or negligently failed to determine the statement's truth.

(Choice B) Libel (written defamation) does not require proof of special harm (ie, monetary loss), so the fact that the general manager suffered no special harm does not defeat his libel claim. In contrast, special harm must be proven for slander (spoken defamation).

(Choice D) A defamation claim can be brought against any person who communicates a false statement to a third party (ie, a person who repeats a defamatory statement is just as liable as the original defamer). Therefore, the newspaper could be liable for defamation even if its article merely reported the employees' comments.

Educational objective: Libel requires proof that the defendant (1) knowingly communicated a false statement about the plaintiff to a third party or (2) negligently failed to determine the statement's falsity (ie, no reasonable care used to determine its truth).



选项正确率统计：A选项 12%，B选项 8%，C选项 53%（正确选项），D选项 25%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

书面诽谤（Libel）是指以书面或其他物理形式出现的诽谤。要在诽谤诉讼中胜诉，原告必须证明以下所有各项：

  • 被告明知关于原告的陈述是虚假的，或因过失未能确定其虚假性（即，未能尽到合理注意义务）。
  • 该类陈述会损害原告的声誉。
  • 被告故意或因过失将该陈述传播给第三方。


如果在审判中，原告未能就支持所有这些要素提出法律上充分的证据（即，没有理性的陪审团会做出有利于原告的裁决），法院应批准被告提出的指示裁决（directed verdict）动议。

在本案中，该报纸在一篇发表的文章中虚假报道了总经理侵吞了数千美元。但是，没有证据表明该报纸知道或因过失未能确定侵吞指控是虚假的，因为它通过咨询前餐厅员工，就该指控尽到了合理注意义务。因此，法院应批准该报纸的指示裁决动议。

(选项A) 由公众人物或官员（如名人、政治家）提起的书面诽谤诉讼，需要明确且有说服力的证据来证明被告发表言论时存在实际恶意——即明知其虚假或鲁莽地漠视其虚假性。但由私人（如本案中的总经理）提起的诉讼，仅需通过优势证据来证明被告知道或因过失未能确定陈述的真实性。

(选项B) 书面诽谤（written defamation）不需要证明特殊损害（即金钱损失），因此总经理没有遭受特殊损害这一事实，并不能使其诽谤诉讼不成立。相比之下，口头诽谤（slander）则必须证明存在特殊损害。

(选项D) 诽谤诉讼可以对向第三方传播虚假陈述的任何人提起（即，重复诽谤性陈述的人与原始诽谤者承担同等责任）。因此，即使报纸的文章只是报道了员工的评论，报纸也可能要为诽谤承担责任。

教学目标：书面诽谤（Libel）要求证明被告（1）明知是关于原告的虚假陈述而向第三方传播，或（2）因过失未能确定陈述的虚假性（即，未尽合理注意义务来确定其真实性）。

References

  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 558 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (elements of defamation).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 580B (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (knowing or negligent statement of falsity).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(a) (judgment as a matter of law).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Defamation (Libel)

Topic: 诽谤罪的过错标准
核心考点：
根据美国宪法第一修正案的要求，当原告是私人人物 (Private Figure)，且涉及公共利益 (Public Concern) 时，原告必须证明被告在陈述的真实性上至少存在过失 (Negligence)。
✅ 正确答案：C

案卷中没有证据表明，该报纸对于侵吞指控的真伪存在过失。

深度解析

本题考查的是诽谤法中关于过错 (Fault) 的举证责任。我们需要分三步来分析：

1. 确定原告身份：
本案中的原告是餐厅总经理。在法律上，他通常被视为私人人物 (Private Figure)，而非公职人员 (Public Official) 或公众人物 (Public Figure)。

2. 确定过错标准：
根据最高法院判例 Gertz v. Robert Welch, Inc.，对于私人原告起诉媒体被告的诽谤案件，各州可以自行设定过错标准，但不能实行严格责任 (Strict Liability)。大多数司法管辖区要求的最低标准是过失 (Negligence)。

这意味着原告必须证明：报纸在核实信息真伪时，没有尽到合理的注意义务。

3. 审视程序 (Directed Verdict)：
题目中提到报纸申请了指示裁决 (Directed Verdict)。这通常发生在一方未能就其主张的某个必要要素提供充分证据时。由于原告（总经理）必须证明被告（报纸）存在过失，而案卷显示“没有证据”表明报纸有过失（例如报纸可能已经采访了员工，尽到了合理调查义务），因此原告未能满足举证责任。

为什么其他选项是错误的？
❌ 选项 A (Actual Malice)
错误原因：标准过高。“实际恶意” (Actual Malice，即明知虚假或鲁莽漠视真相) 是针对公众人物的标准。本案原告是私人，只需证明过失即可。
❌ 选项 B (Special Harm)
错误原因：书面诽谤 (Libel) 通常被视为本身具有损害性，或者至少在许多管辖区不需要证明具体的金钱损失 (Special Damages) 就能确立责任。即使没有特殊损害，也不足以直接导致指示裁决，因为过错要素的缺失才是致命伤。
❌ 选项 D (Republication Rule)
错误原因：这是一个常见的陷阱。法律原则是 "Tale bearers are as bad as tale makers"（传谣者与造谣者同罪）。仅仅证明“文章准确引用了员工的话”并不能免责。如果报纸在引用时没有核实真相（存在过失），它仍然要对传播虚假信息负责。因此，仅凭“准确报道了员工的话”这一证据，不足以让报纸胜诉。
🎓 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)：
在 MBE 诽谤题中，首先判断原告身份（私人 vs. 公众人物）。
  • 如果是公众人物 ➡️ 必须证明 Actual Malice。
  • 如果是私人人物 ➡️ 通常只需证明 Negligence。
如果题目说“没有证据表明被告有过失”，那么私人原告必败。

questions.question:
A well-known movie star was drinking a vineyard's wine at a nightclub. A bottle of the vineyard's wine, with its label plainly showing, was on the table in front of the movie star. An amateur photographer asked the movie star if he could take his picture and the movie star said, "Yes." Subsequently, the photographer sold the photo to the vineyard. The vineyard, without the movie star's consent, used the photo in a wine advertisement in a nationally circulated magazine. The caption below the photo stated, "A movie star enjoys the vineyard's wine."
If the movie star sues the vineyard to recover damages as a result of the vineyard's use of the photograph, will the movie star prevail?

choices.a: No, because the movie star consented to being photographed.
choices.b: No, because the movie star is a public figure.
choices.c: Yes, because the vineyard made commercial use of the photograph.
choices.d: Yes, unless the movie star did, in fact, enjoy the vineyard's wine.

A well-known movie star was drinking a vineyard's wine at a nightclub. A bottle of the vineyard's wine, with its label plainly showing, was on the table in front of the movie star. An amateur photographer asked the movie star if he could take his picture and the movie star said, "Yes." Subsequently, the photographer sold the photo to the vineyard. The vineyard, without the movie star's consent, used the photo in a wine advertisement in a nationally circulated magazine. The caption below the photo stated, "A movie star enjoys the vineyard's wine."

If the movie star sues the vineyard to recover damages as a result of the vineyard's use of the photograph, will the movie star prevail?

一位知名电影明星在一家夜总会饮用某酒庄的葡萄酒。一瓶该酒庄的葡萄酒放在这位电影明星面前的桌子上，酒瓶标签清晰可见。一名业余摄影师问这位电影明星是否可以为他拍照，电影明星回答说：“可以。”随后，该摄影师将照片卖给了该酒庄。该酒庄未经电影明星的同意，在一本全国发行的杂志上将这张照片用于一则葡萄酒广告。照片下方的标题写着：“一位电影明星正在享用本酒庄的葡萄酒。”

如果该电影明星因酒庄使用其照片而起诉酒庄要求损害赔偿，该电影明星是否会胜诉？
options:
A. No, because the movie star consented to being photographed.
不会，因为该电影明星同意被拍照。

B. No, because the movie star is a public figure.
不会，因为该电影明星是公众人物。

C. Yes, because the vineyard made commercial use of the photograph.
会，因为该酒庄将照片用于商业用途。

D. Yes, unless the movie star did, in fact, enjoy the vineyard's wine.
会，除非该电影明星事实上确实喜欢该酒庄的葡萄酒。
data.explanation:
To recover damages for an invasion of privacy claim based on appropriation of name or likeness (ie, misappropriation of the right to publicity), the plaintiff must prove that the defendant:

used the plaintiff's picture , name, or likeness without authorization and obtained a benefit (typically a commercial advantage - eg, advertising) from that use.

Here, the vineyard used the movie star's photo in an advertisement in a nationally circulated magazine. Although the movie star consented to being photographed, he did not authorize the vineyard to use his photo (Choice A). And since the vineyard made commercial use of that photo (wine advertisement) without authorization, the movie star will recover damages from the vineyard.

(Choice B) Public figures have the same right to control the use of their identities as anyone else, so the fact that the movie star is a public figure does not preclude his recovery. Instead, this fact strengthens his claim by establishing the commercial value (ie, benefit) of using his identity.

(Choice D) Truth is a defense to an invasion of privacy claim based on publicity in false light , which requires proof that the defendant published false information about the plaintiff. But truth is no defense here since falsity is not an element of appropriation of name or likeness . Therefore, the movie star will recover even if the photo caption truthfully claimed that he enjoyed the vineyard's wine.

Educational objective: Invasion of privacy based on appropriation of name or likeness requires proof that the defendant (1) used the plaintiff's name, picture, or likeness without his/her authorization and (2) obtained a benefit - typically a commercial advantage.



选项正确率统计：A选项 4%，B选项 2%，C选项 91%（正确选项），D选项 1%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

要在一项基于appropriation of name or likeness（姓名或肖像盗用）的invasion of privacy（侵犯隐私权）索赔中获得损害赔偿，原告必须证明被告：

未经授权使用原告的照片、姓名或肖像，并且通过该使用获得了利益（通常是商业利益——例如广告）。

在本案中，该酒庄在一本全国发行的杂志上将该电影明星的照片用于广告。虽然该电影明星同意被拍照，但他并未授权该酒庄使用其照片（选项A）。并且由于该酒庄未经授权将该照片用于商业用途（葡萄酒广告），该电影明星将从该酒庄获得损害赔偿。

（选项B）公众人物与任何其他人一样，有权控制其身份的使用，因此该电影明星是公众人物这一事实并不妨碍其获得赔偿。相反，这一事实通过确立其身份使用的商业价值（即利益）而加强了他的主张。

（选项D）事实抗辩适用于基于publicity in false light（置于虚假公众印象中）的invasion of privacy索赔，该索赔要求证明被告发布了关于原告的虚假信息。但在此案中，事实并非抗辩理由，因为虚假性不是appropriation of name or likeness的构成要件。因此，即使照片标题如实声称他喜欢该酒庄的葡萄酒，该电影明星仍将获得赔偿。

教学目标：基于appropriation of name or likeness的Invasion of privacy要求证明被告（1）未经授权使用了原告的姓名、照片或肖像，并且（2）获得了利益——通常是商业利益。

References

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 652C (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (appropriation of name or likeness).

MBE 考点解析

侵权法 (Torts) - 隐私权 (Privacy)
⚖️ 核心法律规则 本题考查的是隐私权侵权中的姓名或肖像盗用 (Appropriation of Name or Likeness)。

构成要件：
  1. 被告使用了原告的姓名或肖像；
  2. 未经原告授权 (Unauthorized)；
  3. 为了被告的商业利益 (Commercial Advantage)。
为什么选 C？(逻辑推演)

选项 C 指出“酒庄将照片用于商业用途”，这直接击中了本案的法律核心。

  • 商业使用：酒庄将照片放在全国发行的杂志广告中，目的是为了推销葡萄酒，这显然构成了商业利益。
  • 缺乏授权：虽然电影明星同意被“拍照”，但他并没有同意照片被用于“商业广告”。

在 Appropriation 侵权中，只要证明被告未经许可利用原告的身份获取了商业利益，原告即可胜诉。

🚫 常见陷阱排除
❌ 选项 A：同意的范围 (Scope of Consent)
这是 MBE 常见的干扰项。同意“被拍照”不等于同意“照片被用于商业广告”。同意是有范围限制的。
❌ 选项 B：公众人物 (Public Figure)
公众人物并未放弃对其肖像商业价值的控制权。相反，因为他们的形象具有商业价值（Right of Publicity），这种侵权造成的损失往往更大。
⚠️ 重点警示：选项 D (真相抗辩) 选项 D 认为如果明星“真的喜欢”这酒，酒庄就没事。这是错误的！

真相 (Truth) 是针对诽谤 (Defamation) 或 虚假光环 (False Light) 的抗辩理由。

但在肖像盗用 (Appropriation) 中，无论陈述是否属实，只要你未经允许拿别人的脸去赚钱，就构成侵权。
MBE 解题技巧：
看到“未经同意用于广告”，首先定位 Appropriation。
区分“隐私权”与“名誉权”，不要被“内容真实”所迷惑。

questions.question:
A recently established law school constructed its building in a quiet residential neighborhood. The law school had obtained all the necessary municipal permits for the construction of the building, which included a large clock tower whose clock chimed every hour. The chimes disturbed only one homeowner in the neighborhood, who had purchased her house prior to the construction of the building. The homeowner was abnormally sensitive to ringing sounds, such as bells and sirens, and found the chimes to be extremely annoying.
In a nuisance action by the homeowner against the law school, will the homeowner be likely to prevail?

choices.a: No, because the chimes do not disturb the other residents of the neighborhood.
choices.b: No, because the law school had obtained the requisite municipal permits to erect the clock tower.
choices.c: Yes, because the chimes interfere with the homeowner's use and enjoyment of her property.
choices.d: Yes, because the homeowner purchased her house prior to the construction of the building.

A recently established law school constructed its building in a quiet residential neighborhood. The law school had obtained all the necessary municipal permits for the construction of the building, which included a large clock tower whose clock chimed every hour. The chimes disturbed only one homeowner in the neighborhood, who had purchased her house prior to the construction of the building. The homeowner was abnormally sensitive to ringing sounds, such as bells and sirens, and found the chimes to be extremely annoying.

In a nuisance action by the homeowner against the law school, will the homeowner be likely to prevail?

一所新成立的法学院在一片宁静的住宅区内建造了其教学楼。该法学院已获得所有必要的市政许可来建造该建筑，其中包括一个每小时报时的巨大钟楼。钟声只打扰了社区中的一位房主，她是在该建筑建造之前购买其房屋的。这位房主对铃声和警报声等鸣响声异常敏感，并觉得钟声极其烦人。

在该房主对法学院提起的妨害诉讼中，房主是否可能胜诉？
options:
A. No, because the chimes do not disturb the other residents of the neighborhood.
不会，因为钟声并未打扰到社区的其他居民。

B. No, because the law school had obtained the requisite municipal permits to erect the clock tower.
不会，因为法学院已获得建造钟楼所需的市政许可。

C. Yes, because the chimes interfere with the homeowner's use and enjoyment of her property.
会，因为钟声妨碍了房主对其财产的使用和享用。

D. Yes, because the homeowner purchased her house prior to the construction of the building.
会，因为房主在该建筑建造之前就已购买了她的房屋。
data.explanation:
Nuisance can be either public (interfering with a right common to the general public) OR private (interfering with a private property right - as alleged here). Liability for private nuisance arises when the defendant's interference with the plaintiff's use and enjoyment of his/her property is both:
  • substantial - offensive, annoying, or intolerable to a normal person in the community and
  • unreasonable - the severity of the plaintiff's harm outweighs the utility of the defendant's conduct.
An interference is not substantial if the plaintiff's abnormal sensitivity causes him/her to find the interference offensive, annoying, or intolerable when a normal person in the community would not.

Here, the law school interfered with the homeowner's use and enjoyment of her property by constructing a large clock tower whose clock chimed every hour. But since the homeowner was abnormally sensitive to ringing sounds, she was the only one who found the chimes extremely annoying when no other residents were disturbed. Therefore, the interference was not substantial and the homeowner's nuisance action will likely fail (Choice C).

(Choice B) Although compliance with zoning regulations (eg, obtaining municipal permits) helps show that the defendant's interference was not unreasonable, it is not a defense to nuisance. Instead, the homeowner's claim will fail because no other residents were disturbed by the chimes (no substantial interference).

(Choice D) Courts may consider priority in time (ie, whether the plaintiff came to the nuisance) when determining if a nuisance is actionable. Here, the homeowner's nuisance claim is actionable since she purchased her house before the clock tower was built. However, she will only prevail on this claim if she proves that the law school's interference was both substantial and unreasonable.

Educational objective: An interference with a plaintiff's use and enjoyment of his/her property is not substantial (and will not support a nuisance claim) if the plaintiff's abnormal sensitivity causes him/her to find that interference offensive, annoying, or intolerable when a normal person in the community would not.



选项正确率统计：A选项 86%（正确选项），B选项 0%，C选项 11%，D选项 0%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

妨害可分为公共妨害（干涉公众共同享有的权利）或私人妨害（干涉私人财产权——如此处所主张的）。当被告对原告使用和享用其财产的干涉同时满足以下两点时，私人妨害的法律责任即告成立：
  • 实质性——对社区中的正常人而言具有攻击性、令人烦扰或无法忍受，并且
  • 不合理性——原告所受损害的严重程度超过了被告行为的功用。
如果原告的异常敏感导致其认为该干涉具有攻击性、令人烦扰或无法忍受，而社区中的正常人则不会如此认为，那么这种干涉就不具有实质性。

在本案中，法学院建造了一个每小时报时的大钟楼，从而干涉了房主对其财产的使用和享用。但由于该房主对鸣响声异常敏感，当其他居民未受打扰时，只有她觉得钟声极其烦人。因此，该干涉不具有实质性，房主的妨害诉讼很可能会失败（选项C）。

（选项B）尽管遵守区划法规（例如，获得市政许可）有助于表明被告的干涉并非不合理，但这并不能作为妨害的抗辩理由。相反，房主的诉求之所以会失败，是因为没有其他居民被钟声打扰（即不存在实质性干涉）。

（选项D）在确定妨害行为是否可诉时，法院可能会考虑时间上的优先性（即原告是否“自投妨害”）。在本案中，房主的妨害诉求是可诉的，因为她是在钟楼建成前购买其房屋的。但是，她只有在证明法学院的干涉既具有实质性又不合理的情况下，才能在诉讼中胜诉。

教学目标：如果原告的异常敏感性导致其认为某项干涉具有攻击性、令人烦扰或无法忍受，而社区中的正常人并不会如此认为，那么该项对原告使用和享用其财产的干涉则不具有实质性（并且不能支持妨害诉求）。

References

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 821D (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (private nuisance).

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 821F (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (substantial interference required).

MBE 考点解析

Torts: Private Nuisance
核心法律规则

本题考查的是私人妨害 (Private Nuisance) 中的核心要素：实质性干涉 (Substantial Interference)。

法律规定，要构成私人妨害，被告的行为必须是对原告使用和享用其财产的“实质性且不合理”的干涉。

⚖️
客观标准 (Objective Standard)：
判断干涉是否具有“实质性”，必须以社区中的正常人 (Normal Person / Average Person) 为标准，而不是以原告的主观感受为标准。
案情关键点分析
  • 🚫 干扰源： 法学院钟楼每小时的钟声。
  • 👤 原告特征： 对声音异常敏感 (Abnormally Sensitive)。
  • 🏘️ 社区反应： 钟声仅打扰了这一位房主，其他居民未受影响。
选项深度解析
选项 A (正确)

"不会胜诉，因为钟声并未打扰到社区的其他居民。"

解析：这是对“客观标准”的直接应用。既然钟声没有打扰到社区里的其他人，说明这种干涉对于“正常人”来说并非不可忍受。原告之所以感到痛苦，完全是因为她自身的异常敏感性 (Hypersensitivity)。法律不保护因自身特质而产生的过度敏感，因此不构成实质性干涉。

选项 C (常见陷阱)

"会胜诉，因为钟声妨碍了房主对其财产的使用..."

解析：虽然事实上确实妨碍了这位房主，但在法律上，这种妨碍必须达到“实质性”标准。由于是原告的特殊体质导致了妨碍，而非被告行为本身对大众具有攻击性，因此法律上的因果关系不成立。

选项 B (错误理由)

"不会胜诉，因为已获得市政许可..."

解析：获得区划许可 (Zoning permits) 只是证明被告行为具有一定合理性的证据，但不是针对妨害诉讼的绝对抗辩理由 (Absolute Defense)。即使合法合规，如果对邻居造成了实质性且不合理的干扰，依然可能构成妨害。本题原告败诉的根本原因不是因为被告有许可证，而是因为原告太敏感。

选项 D (无关因素)

"会胜诉，因为房主先购买了房屋..."

解析：这涉及"Coming to the nuisance" (自投妨害) 的概念。虽然原告先住在这里对她有利，但这只是法院考虑的一个因素，并非决定性因素。更重要的是，无论谁先来后到，如果干扰本身不构成“实质性干涉”，诉讼就无法成立。

💡 MBE 考试通关秘籍

在处理 Nuisance (妨害) 题目时，一旦看到题目描述原告：

  • "Abnormally sensitive" (异常敏感)
  • "Unusually susceptible" (异常易受影响)
  • 从事特殊精细业务 (如在震动旁的晶圆厂)
警铃应立即响起！ 🚨
这通常意味着实质性干涉 (Substantial Interference) 这一要素缺失，原告极大概率会败诉。

© MBE 备考助手 | Torts 篇

questions.question:
A company operates a factory that requires the use of very high voltage electricity. A man owns property adjacent to the company's plant where he has attempted to carry on a business that requires the use of sensitive electronic equipment. The effectiveness of the man's electronic equipment is impaired by electrical interference arising from the high voltage currents used in the company's plant. The man has complained to the company several times, with no result. There is no way that the company, by taking reasonable precautions, can avoid the interference with the man's operation that arises from the high voltage currents necessary to the company's operation.
In the man's action against the company to recover damages for the economic loss caused to him by the electrical interference, will the man prevail?

choices.a: No, because the man's harm was purely economic and did not arise from physical harm to his person or property.
choices.b: No, unless the company caused a substantial and unreasonable interference with the man's business.
choices.c: Yes, because the company's activity is abnormally dangerous.
choices.d: Yes, for loss suffered by the man after the company was made aware of the harm its activity was causing to the man.

data.questionStem:
Q83185

A company operates a factory that requires the use of very high voltage electricity. A man owns property adjacent to the company's plant where he has attempted to carry on a business that requires the use of sensitive electronic equipment. The effectiveness of the man's electronic equipment is impaired by electrical interference arising from the high voltage currents used in the company's plant. The man has complained to the company several times, with no result. There is no way that the company, by taking reasonable precautions, can avoid the interference with the man's operation that arises from the high voltage currents necessary to the company's operation.

In the man's action against the company to recover damages for the economic loss caused to him by the electrical interference, will the man prevail?

一家公司经营着一家需要使用超高压电的工厂。一名男子在该公司的工厂旁拥有一处房产，他试图在此经营一项需要使用精密电子设备的业务。该男子电子设备的效能因公司工厂使用的高压电流产生的电磁干扰而受损。该男子已多次向公司投诉，但均无结果。公司无法通过采取合理的预防措施来避免其运营所需的高压电流对该男子业务造成的干扰。

在该男子对该公司提起的诉讼中，要求赔偿因电磁干扰给他造成的经济损失，该男子是否会胜诉？
options:
A. No, because the man's harm was purely economic and did not arise from physical harm to his person or property.
不会，因为该男子的损害纯属经济损失，并非由其人身或财产的物理伤害引起。

B. No, unless the company caused a substantial and unreasonable interference with the man's business.
不会，除非该公司对该男子的业务造成了实质性且不合理的干扰。

C. Yes, because the company's activity is abnormally dangerous.
会，因为该公司的活动属于异常危险活动。

D. Yes, for loss suffered by the man after the company was made aware of the harm its activity was causing to the man.
会，对于在该公司被告知其活动对该男子造成损害后，该男子所遭受的损失可以获得赔偿。
data.explanation:
A plaintiff can recover damages for economic loss and other injuries related to a private nuisance. To recover such damages, the plaintiff must prove that the defendant's interference with the plaintiff's use and enjoyment of his/her property was both:

substantial - offensive, annoying, or intolerable to a normal person in the community and unreasonable - the severity of the plaintiff's harm outweighs the utility of the defendant's conduct.

An interference is not substantial if harm only results from the plaintiff's hypersensitivity (eg, abnormal aversion to the normal ringing of nearby church bells) or abnormal use of his/her own property (eg, sensitive photographic film harmed by heat from nearby factory).

Here, the company interfered with the use and enjoyment of the man's property through high-voltage electricity that impaired the sensitive electronic equipment required for his business (an abnormal use of the man's property). Therefore, the man will not recover economic damages for the company's interference with his business unless he can show that the interference was substantial - eg, that the high-voltage electricity interfered with the normal use of his property - and unreasonable.

(Choice A) Negligence requires proof of physical harm before a plaintiff can recover for economic loss, but nuisance allows a plaintiff to recover for pure economic loss (ie, economic loss not arising from physical harm). Therefore, the man's lack of physical harm does not preclude his recovery for economic loss based on nuisance.

(Choice C) The use of high-voltage electricity may be an abnormally dangerous activity - ie, an uncommon activity in the community that creates a foreseeable and highly significant risk of physical harm that cannot be eliminated by reasonable care. But the company would not be liable for engaging in that activity since the man's harm was caused by electrical interference - not the abnormal danger of that activity (eg, electric shock).

(Choice D) Private nuisance does not require proof that the defendant was aware of the harm caused by his/her activity. Therefore, if the company's interference was substantial and unreasonable, the man could recover for losses suffered before and after the company was made aware of his harm.

Educational objective: Private nuisance requires proof that the defendant substantially and unreasonably interfered with the plaintiff's use and enjoyment of his/her property. An interference is not substantial if the plaintiff's harm results from his/her hypersensitivity or abnormal use of the property.



选项正确率统计：A选项 29%，B选项 61%（正确选项），C选项 2%，D选项 6%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

原告可以就与私人妨害 (private nuisance) 相关的经济损失和其他损害获得赔偿。为获得此类损害赔偿，原告必须证明被告对其财产使用和享有的干扰 (interference) 同时满足以下两点：

实质性 (substantial)——对社区中的普通人而言是冒犯性的、令人烦恼的或无法忍受的，并且不合理 (unreasonable)——原告所受损害的严重程度超过了被告行为的功用。

如果损害仅由原告的超敏反应 (plaintiff's hypersensitivity)（例如，对附近教堂正常钟声的异常厌恶）或其对自有财产的异常使用 (abnormal use of his/her own property)（例如，敏感的照相胶片被附近工厂的热量损坏）造成，则该干扰不具有实质性。

在本案中，公司通过高压电干扰了该男子对其财产的使用和享有，损害了其业务所需的精密电子设备（属于对该男子财产的异常使用）。因此，该男子将无法就公司对其业务的干扰获得经济损失赔偿，除非他能证明该干扰是实质性的——例如，高压电干扰了其财产的正常使用——并且是不合理的。

（选项 A）过失侵权要求原告在获得经济损失赔偿前，必须证明存在物理伤害，但妨害侵权允许原告就纯粹的经济损失（即非由物理伤害引起的经济损失）获得赔偿。因此，该男子缺乏物理伤害并不妨碍他依据妨害侵权来获得经济损失赔偿。

（选项 C）使用高压电可能属于异常危险活动——即社区中不常见的、会造成可预见的、极大的物理伤害风险，且无法通过合理注意消除的活动。但是，公司不会因从事该活动而承担责任，因为该男子的损害是由电磁干扰造成的，而非该活动的异常危险（例如，电击）本身造成的。

（选项 D）私人妨害不要求证明被告知晓其活动造成的损害。因此，如果公司的干扰是实质性且不合理的，那么无论是在公司被告知其损害之前还是之后，该男子所遭受的损失都可以获得赔偿。

教学目标：私人妨害要求证明被告对原告的财产使用和享有造成了实质性且不合理的干扰。如果原告的损害是因其自身的超敏反应或对财产的异常使用所致，则该干扰不具有实质性。

References

  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 822 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (private nuisance liability).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 821F (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (substantial harm requirement).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 826 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (unreasonable interference requirement).
  • Postal Tel.-Cable Co. v. Pac. Gas & Elec. Co., 202 Cal. 382, 385 (1927) (using sensitive electrical equipment is an abnormal use of property).
